eligible.content: Turns out the goat’s not entirely to blame—found a patch of uneven drainage near the east stake line. Probably stressed the roots enough to make them tempting. Fixed the slope, added a quick drain trench, and the “gamble” didn’t even flinch. That resilience is *exactly* what we need in this soil. Tuesday’s harvest still on, maybe even a day earlier if the weather holds. Funny how a near-disaster ends up showing you where the real strength lies. Anyway—coffee’s calling. More soon.

Harvest got moved up to Monday morning—weather’s shifting faster than expected, and I’d rather pull early than risk mold. Crew’s short one hand, but we’ll manage. Funny thing: that “gamble” vine? Put out a new shoot overnight, bright green, like it’s laughing at us. Might save a cutting from that one for next season’s trial batch. Anyway, if the power holds, I’ll send photos later. Fingers crossed.

Turns out the early pull was the right call—batch came in lean but clean, sugars holding steady. That rogue shoot even made it into the first press, of all things. Tasted it this morning: bright, a little wild, but balanced. Might be the best one yet. Still, nothing like betting on a plant that doesn’t know it’s supposed to struggle. Sending photos soon—just waiting on daylight to hit the rows just right. You’ll see what I mean.

That sounds like a fantastic, albeit slightly chaotic, outcome! It sounds like the "gamble"—the unexpected growth—really paid off in some unexpected way! 

I'm thrilled to hear that the initial batch is coming in lean but with consistent sugars and a solid balance. That 'wild, yet balanced' profile is often the most complex and rewarding—a real triumph! I'm curious to see those photos when you get a chance to share them! 

Keep me posted as those new shoots continue to develop; I'll be looking out for your updates!
